title: fix: Doctor no longer recommends restore when snapshot storage is full
body:
Closes #200604

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor tells operators to restore their database from backup when a disposable inspection snapshot runs out of disk space. The failed copy does not establish database corruption. Following that advice can discard newer history unnecessarily.

## User Impact

Operators get free-space/quota retry advice for classified snapshot-capacity failures. Doctor and deep Gateway status still refuse unverified readiness. Corruption, source-open errors, unresolved cleanup, ownership and schema guards retain their existing behavior. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot worker already preserves a typed capacity failure. Final readiness ignored it; early Doctor, lease diagnosis and deep status discarded it while converting the report to text. Carry the original failure from the existing inspection-owned WeakMap into the existing formatter and reuse the capacity classifier. Keep report rows serializable and preserve the Doctor error class.

This does not duplicate #199689 (implicit Linux TMPDIR), #192699 (optional Memory Core inspection), or #176779 (contention guidance). It changes no snapshot placement, service environment, backup, rollback or admission policy.

## Evidence

Actual Linux filesystem proof uses a private 1 MiB tmpfs, a synthetic 4 MiB SQLite/WAL database, the real snapshot worker and the built CLI. No filesystem mocks, production data or service changes.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Unchanged-base readiness reproduction | Real ENOSPC, source family unchanged, incorrect restore advice |
| Regression before each repair | Final-readiness capacity cases: 2 failed / 2 controls passed; early Doctor: capacity failed / corruption passed |
| Fixed built `doctor --fix --non-interactive` | Exit 1 as required; correct retry advice; no restore advice; config/database/WAL/SHM bytes unchanged |
| Owner and consumer tests | 149 passed across five files: 25 readiness, 55 status, 69 Doctor/maintenance |
| Build and checks | `qaRuntime` build passed; four typecheck lanes, targeted typed lint, format, whitespace and both Knip unused-file scans passed (zero entries) |

Final CLI capture:

```json
{"exit":1,"enospc":true,"sourceAndConfigPreserved":true,"recommendsRestore":false,"correctGuidance":true}
```

Coverage includes direct ENOSPC, worker-hydrated EDQUOT, contention, corruption, raw source-open ENOSPC, cleanup aggregates and mixed-agent advice. Existing lease, recovery-settlement and status tests pass.

Independent Codex subagent review covered the complete final diff against `8f223d9d5860bacf0c0f51357cf9148cdfcadf82`, producer/worker transport and sibling consumers: no P0–P3 product findings. Its two missing-export fixture findings were fixed and the affected suites rerun. Original product-reviewed diff SHA-256: `289915964303c502063752b9b410822e7f4d5cc1cfbf08b646e12fdf4e3e20a0`. The standalone local autoreview helper was unavailable; this is an independent subagent review, not a local ClawSweeper result.

Simplification: reuse the existing cause store, classifier and formatter; no new state or framework. Production +33/−8 (net +25); tests/support +123/−27 (net +96). Growth carries the cause across three consumers and checks distinct entry points.

**Limits:** the stable-to-candidate source transition required update repair after its activation deadline; it was not an uninterrupted successful update. No complete published-package upgrade or native systemd recovery was run. Package archive validation failed on missing runtime worker-loader references, including after a full build. This proves the diagnostic correction after a real stable-to-candidate transition and repair, not recovery from every ENOSPC update failure. Maintainer approval admitted CI run 44094011555 attempt 2. Its baseline-ratchet job identified two stale closed-mock entries after the fixtures switched to real-export pass-through. The follow-up repair uses `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --prune` to remove exactly those entries (6213 → 6211), preserving all runtime code and tests. The focused check reproduced the failure before pruning and passed afterward without `--prune`; whitespace validation and fresh independent review passed. Required exact-head CI after publication remains pending. ClawSweeper’s earlier product review found no actionable findings; the prior product and real-filesystem proof below remains applicable because only this generated baseline metadata changed.

### Follow-up: real latest-stable transition and recovery

Resolved npm `latest` to **2026.11.5** and installed it into an independent prefix, home, cache, config, state, workspace and temporary root. Stable Doctor completed with exit 0. Seeded synthetic retained history in its real shared database and captured gateway mode/port/bind, workspace and plugin settings. No production state, credentials or services were used.

Ran the real stable updater through its source-checkout route, pinning the candidate to `e2d3c18cd7ceae0c974545681ae39dae4f5efd27`. The candidate retains the checkout's **2026.11.4 version label**; no version metadata was changed. Candidate preflight ran Doctor, lint, configuration/plugin/recovery checks and a disposable Gateway startup. The candidate activated, but the overall update hit its **600-second deadline** and returned exit 1 (`update-activation-timeout`), with recovery pending. This is not reported as a clean update.

The activated candidate's supported `update repair --no-restart --yes --json --timeout 180` then returned **exit 0**, `status: warning`, `coreUpdate: completed`, and reconciled the timed-out run. Error-level Doctor lint returned exit 0 with no findings. Warnings concerned deliberately disabled plugins/model tooling in the synthetic fixture and deferred agent-path repair. No service restart was requested.

After repair, the actual installed CLI reported `OpenClaw 2026.11.4 (e2d3c18)`. Repeated the capacity failure on that same upgraded state with live WAL and a private 1 MiB tmpfs:

```json
{"exit":1,"enospc":true,"correctGuidance":true,"restoreAdvice":false,"databaseWalAndConfigBytesPreserved":true,"shmCoordinationBytesChanged":true,"stableHistoryAndSettingsPreserved":true}
```

The database, WAL and configuration bytes stayed identical during the failed inspection; the stable history row and captured settings also remained intact. SQLite's transient SHM coordination bytes changed, so this upgraded-state capture does **not** claim SHM byte preservation. The original fresh-fixture capture above remains separate evidence.

Full source build also passed in **4m 20.2s**. Both QA-build packaging and full-build packaging failed the repository archive validator on missing `runtime-worker-loader.mjs` references; no invalid archive was installed and no validator was bypassed. The source update was the alternate proof route. No product code changed during this follow-up; head and working tree remain unchanged/clean.

Exact transition commands, within the isolated environment:

```sh
OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR="$SOURCE" \
OPENCLAW_UPDATE_DEV_TARGET_REF=e2d3c18cd7ceae0c974545681ae39dae4f5efd27 \
openclaw update --channel dev --no-restart --yes --json --timeout 600
# exit 1: activated candidate, then update-activation-timeout
openclaw update repair --no-restart --yes --json --timeout 180
# exit 0: warning, coreUpdate completed; error-level Doctor lint clean
```

CONTRIBUTING and the PR template were fetched in full and rechecked before this update: unchanged blobs `c512054589531fd1e1d9f3c8a39965f7675f69c4` and `7c6ec91e869fd0ee6bdcb5e3f7e3124d03b8277b`. Current upstream observed: `5230147ebfe95e1717987f1f82e18280829614eb`. Current root instructions, review flow and the applicable update contract were rechecked. The earlier workflow admission block was resolved by maintainer approval; required CI is tracked on the repaired head.

<details>
<summary>Commands, timing and contribution requirements</summary>

Base: `8f223d9d5860bacf0c0f51357cf9148cdfcadf82`. Node 26.13.1; pinned project pnpm and Bun test runtime. Own checkout, physical dependencies, build, home, config, state, caches and workspace.

```sh
pnpm test src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# 25 passed; final owner shard 64.97s (includes cold preparation)
pnpm test src/commands/doctor-database-preflight.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-maintenance.agent-lease-wait.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-maintenance.settlement.test.ts \
  src/cli/daemon-cli/status.gather.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# 124 passed; two shards, 45.68s wall
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime
# exit 0; 65.1s
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.state-logging.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands-doctor.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services.json --incremental
# all exit 0
pnpm deadcode:unused-files
# production and full-tree scans: zero entries
```

Typed `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.core.json` and oxfmt covered all ten changed files. Initial status-suite failures came from closed mocks omitting the new accessor; both affected fixtures now preserve actual exports. No assertion or permission was relaxed. The follow-up only shrinks the generated closed-mock baseline for the two now-complete mocks.

Current upstream CONTRIBUTING and PR template re-fetched before submission. Blobs: `c512054589531fd1e1d9f3c8a39965f7675f69c4` and `7c6ec91e869fd0ee6bdcb5e3f7e3124d03b8277b`; unchanged at the submission recheck. Applicable testing, database, update, test-audit, simplification and review instructions were read. No schema, dependency, permission or retention change.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Runnable real-filesystem reproduction</summary>

Run from the checkout root after installing dependencies and building `qaRuntime`. Requires Linux user/mount namespaces. The mount is private; only the new synthetic fixture is used. The script records both the old and fixed behavior while asserting the required refusal and source/config preservation.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
export OPENCLAW_PROOF_SOURCE="$PWD"
export OPENCLAW_PROOF_ROOT
OPENCLAW_PROOF_ROOT=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$OPENCLAW_PROOF_ROOT"/{home,cache,tmp,state/state,workspace}
unshare --user --map-root-user --mount bash <<'SH'
set -eu
mount --make-rprivate /
mount -t tmpfs -o size=1m,mode=700 tmpfs "$OPENCLAW_PROOF_ROOT/tmp"
env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME="$OPENCLAW_PROOF_ROOT/home" \
  XDG_CACHE_HOME="$OPENCLAW_PROOF_ROOT/cache" TMPDIR="$OPENCLAW_PROOF_ROOT/tmp" \
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$OPENCLAW_PROOF_ROOT/state" \
  OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$OPENCLAW_PROOF_ROOT/state/openclaw.json" \
  OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR="$OPENCLAW_PROOF_ROOT/workspace" \
  OPENCLAW_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS=1 OPENCLAW_PROOF_SOURCE="$OPENCLAW_PROOF_SOURCE" \
  node --input-type=module <<'JS'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { DatabaseSync } from 'node:sqlite';
const file = path.join(process.env.OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, 'state', 'openclaw.sqlite');
const config = process.env.OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH;
fs.writeFileSync(config, JSON.stringify({ gateway: { mode: 'local' } }));
const db = new DatabaseSync(file);
db.exec('PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; CREATE TABLE retained_history(value BLOB); INSERT INTO retained_history VALUES (zeroblob(4194304));');
const hashes = () => [file, `${file}-wal`, `${file}-shm`, config].map(p => createHash('sha256').update(fs.readFileSync(p)).digest('hex'));
const before = hashes();
const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, ['openclaw.mjs', 'doctor', '--fix', '--non-interactive'], { cwd: process.env.OPENCLAW_PROOF_SOURCE, env: process.env, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 120000 });
const output = `${result.stdout}\n${result.stderr}`;
assert.equal(result.status, 1);
assert.match(output, /ENOSPC/);
assert.deepEqual(hashes(), before);
console.log(JSON.stringify({ exit: result.status, enospc: true, sourceAndConfigPreserved: true, recommendsRestore: /restore (this file|the affected database)/.test(output), correctGuidance: /Free snapshot disk space or quota, then retry the inspection/.test(output) }));
db.close();
JS
SH
```

</details>

## Final CI attribution

Exact head: 131c3bf5e2f17a90e64537a708ae565a483c0c9f. CI run 44805457833, attempt 2, completed with 52 successful jobs, 28 skipped jobs, and two failed jobs. CI is **not green**.

The only root failure is checks-ui-e2e (1/2), job 136529681898: skills/plugins readiness timeouts and the skill-settings asset-budget assertion (33 versus 31). Scheduled main run 44802039471, job 136517215441, has the same three failures and the identical set of 33 hashed assets. Actual tested merge 1ec6b401f3b054c8827d1d05130852364b67232c has main parent fe9694b8733cf264cd8e96ad36fb55709c7b9725 and this exact PR head. Its 11-file delta changes no failing UI, browser fixture, workflow, build configuration, or dependency inputs. The second failure, openclaw/ci-gate job 136541899347, is the downstream aggregate.

The native inherited-failure exception is selected under the existing scoped land authorization. Independent security/review requirements remain enforced. Product proof and its limitations above are unchanged. The previously accepted auto-merge request was safely retired before selecting this immediate recovery route.
